body.statement: Whenever \(K_\delta(P)>0\), one may choose \(B\) so that \(P_t\) is a legal two-sided dominated Bernoulli submodel with bounded finite-partition score \(S_B\), and the two one-sided derivatives of \(\Psi_\delta(P_t)\) at zero are \(0\) and \(\delta\mathbb E_P[\tau(X)\mathbf 1_B(X)]\ne0\). Thus signed cancellation of \(\mathbb E_P[\tau(X)\mathbf 1\{e(X)=c\}]\) cannot restore differentiability.
body.justification: A legal localized score closes the necessity direction without perturbing binary probabilities outside their support.
body.gap: Hirano and Porter provide the generic nondifferentiable-experiment implication; the proposed finite-partition tangent embeds that obstruction in the exact binary-treatment cap model.
body.consumer: The construction supplies a falsification experiment for any claimed regular estimator at an outcome-relevant cap atom.
